notes: Historical facts (FY2023-2025): Net sales and operating income are taken directly from Corning’s Consolidated Statements of Income; EBIT is modeled as operating income (GAAP). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000124/glw-20251231.htm))

Historical D&A and capex: D&A is modeled as depreciation plus amortization of purchased intangibles from the cash flow statement; capex is modeled as “Capital expenditures” from the cash flow statement (absolute positive amounts). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000124/glw-20251231.htm))

Working capital (NWC) definition: NWC is modeled as Total current assets minus Total current liabilities (includes cash and cash equivalents; excludes non-current working capital items). FY2023 is sourced from the FY2024 10-K balance sheet. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000124/glw-20251231.htm))

Forecast construction: forecast revenue uses the provided revenue_growth series chained from FY2025 net sales; forecast EBIT uses EBIT margin applied to forecast revenue; D&A/capex/NWC use the provided % of sales ratios.
Base-case discounting: WACC (0.085) is a modeled assumption for a DCF input package; it is not sourced from a single canonical provider in this run (see comps section for proxy multiples).

Terminal method: terminal_method is set to “average” and therefore uses both terminal_growth and terminal_exit_ebitda_multiple; the exact averaging implementation is left to the downstream DCF engine.
NOLs: NOL balance was not extracted reliably from the available filing excerpts here, so nol_balance is set to null; nol_utilization_pct is kept at 0.80 as a base modeling utilization assumption.

Comps limitation: EV/NTM revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA fields are populated using publicly shown EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA multiples from StockAnalysis snapshots; those sources do not explicitly label the numerator/denominator as NTM, so these are treated as proxies rather than strictly NTM consensus metrics. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/cohr/statistics/))

catalysts: Execution on the upgraded Springboard growth trajectory and delivery of incremental annualized sales targets referenced in management’s FY2025 release. ([investor.corning.com](https://investor.corning.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2026/Corning-Announces-Outstanding-2025-Financial-Results-1--Upgrades-Springboard-Plan-for-Faster-Sales-Growth-on-Significantly-Enhanced-Financial-Profile/default.aspx))

Follow-through on data-center/AI fiber-related demand signals (including the multi-year agreement announcement referenced in the FY2025 results release). ([investor.corning.com](https://investor.corning.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2026/Corning-Announces-Outstanding-2025-Financial-Results-1--Upgrades-Springboard-Plan-for-Faster-Sales-Growth-on-Significantly-Enhanced-Financial-Profile/default.aspx))
Further operating margin expansion if pricing/mix and cost actions persist through the forecast horizon. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000124/glw-20251231.htm))
company_overview: Corning operates across telecom/network products, high-performance glass, advanced optical materials, ceramic substrates, and multiple specialty materials applications. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000124/glw-20251231.htm))
In FY2025, net sales were $15.629B with operating income of $2.279B (GAAP). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000124/glw-20251231.htm))

Corning’s financial trajectory has improved materially in 2025 vs. 2023-2024, with higher operating income and cash flow generation. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000124/glw-20251231.htm))
current_context: Corning reported FY2025 GAAP net sales of $15.63B (+19% YoY) and GAAP operating cash flow of $2.70B; it also provided an outlook for accelerating YoY growth in Q1 2026. ([investor.corning.com](https://investor.corning.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2026/Corning-Announces-Outstanding-2025-Financial-Results-1--Upgrades-Springboard-Plan-for-Faster-Sales-Growth-on-Significantly-Enhanced-Financial-Profile/default.aspx))

Management upgraded its Springboard plan, adding incremental annualized sales by end-2026 and end-2028 (announced with the FY2025 results release). ([investor.corning.com](https://investor.corning.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2026/Corning-Announces-Outstanding-2025-Financial-Results-1--Upgrades-Springboard-Plan-for-Faster-Sales-Growth-on-Significantly-Enhanced-Financial-Profile/default.aspx))

The FY2025 earnings release emphasized continued momentum into 2026, including Q1 expectations for core sales growth in the mid-teens range. ([investor.corning.com](https://investor.corning.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2026/Corning-Announces-Outstanding-2025-Financial-Results-1--Upgrades-Springboard-Plan-for-Faster-Sales-Growth-on-Significantly-Enhanced-Financial-Profile/default.aspx))
investment_highlights: Base-case modeling reflects continued profitability expansion (EBIT margin rising from the 2023 level to stabilize at ~low-to-mid 0.1s in the outer forecast years). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000124/glw-20251231.htm))

Forecast revenue growth decelerates from FY2025’s strong growth into a more conservative mid-single-digit profile, aligning with a mature/structural demand but cyclical end-market risk. ([investor.corning.com](https://investor.corning.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2026/Corning-Announces-Outstanding-2025-Financial-Results-1--Upgrades-Springboard-Plan-for-Faster-Sales-Growth-on-Significantly-Enhanced-Financial-Profile/default.aspx))

D&A and capex are modeled as percentages of sales near recent levels, consistent with an industrial/materials asset base that has been actively managed for efficiency. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000124/glw-20251231.htm))

Net working capital intensity is assumed to stabilize/slightly improve vs. FY2024, consistent with the observed decline in NWC%Sales in FY2025. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000124/glw-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Cyclical weakness in telecom and display end markets could pressure revenue growth and margins below base-case assumptions.

Foreign exchange and tax items (including cross-border dynamics and uncertain tax positions) can introduce volatility in reported GAAP earnings and effective tax behavior. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000124/glw-20251231.htm))
Capex execution risk and working capital swings could reduce free cash flow vs. modeled NWC and capex ratios.

valuation_summary: The DCF base case uses FY2023-2025 GAAP fundamentals and assumes gradual revenue growth deceleration with margin stabilization, producing a conservative terminal economics set (terminal_growth and exit multiple).

Selected peer multiples provide a reality check on the implied valuation range; however, note that EV/NTM revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA are proxied using EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA from public snapshots (not explicitly labeled NTM in the sources).
